input: Schedule a tai chi class at the community center

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether the user wants to find and join an existing class, create/organize a new one, or book a space changes the entire plan.
Whether this is for the user alone, a group of friends, or a broader public class affects registration steps and coordination needed.
The specific community center and its existing tai chi offerings determines what options are available and what contact is needed.
The user's availability (days, times) is a hard limit that filters which class slots are viable.
The user's experience level (beginner, intermediate, advanced) determines what type of class or instructor is appropriate.
Knowing how registration works (online, phone, in-person) and whether the user has already contacted the center shapes the immediate next action.
Understanding what the user considers 'done' — a one-time session vs. a recurring weekly commitment — affects how the plan is structured.

gold.taskTitle: Schedule a tai chi class at the community center
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to arrange or sign up for a tai chi class held at their local community center.

questions.title: Are you joining an existing class or organizing a new one?
questions.description: Determines whether the task is about signing up as a participant or creating/coordinating a class from scratch.

questions.title: Is this just for you or a group of people?
questions.description: Clarifies whether the user needs a single registration or must coordinate multiple participants.

questions.title: Which community center do you have in mind?
questions.description: Identifies the specific facility so the correct schedule, contacts, and offerings can be referenced.

questions.title: Which days and times work best for you?
questions.description: Pinpoints the user's availability as a hard filter for choosing among class options.

questions.title: What is your current tai chi experience level?
questions.description: Ensures the class type (beginner, intermediate, advanced) matches the user's background.

questions.title: Have you already contacted the center, or is that still needed?
questions.description: Establishes the starting point so the plan begins at the right step — research, outreach, or actual registration.

questions.title: Are you looking for a one-time session or recurring classes?
questions.description: Defines what 'done' looks like — a single drop-in booking versus a multi-week enrollment commitment.
